First, on voluntary disclosure: I recommend we proceed with a voluntary disclosure. The $275,000 reconciliation I completed with controllership gives us a concrete, verified figure, and getting ahead of this proactively positions us more favorably than waiting for DOJ to uncover it through document production. Second, on the repayment amount: I recommend we commit to the full $275,000 as the improperly identified amount. That figure is supported by the ledger reconciliation and matching invoices and has been confirmed with controllership as of yesterday. Third, on the executive-interview protocol: given Jordan's confirmation that the implicated VP has separate counsel and will not participate without written consent from that counsel, I recommend we build in a contingent protocol — we schedule the interview with reasonable notice but condition it on receiving that written consent, and we set an outer deadline so we're not indefinitely delayed. We should also identify a fallback witness who can speak to the relevant distributor relationships if the VP remains unavailable. Those are my final recommendations on all three open items, Elena.

transcript.text: Thank you, Elena. As employment counsel, here are my final recommendations on each open item. First, on voluntary disclosure: I recommend yes. The employment-law exposure here is significant — if DOJ uncovers improper commission payments through document production rather than through our own disclosure, it complicates our ability to manage personnel decisions, including any disciplinary action against the implicated VP and others involved. Getting ahead of this proactively gives us more control over the employment ramifications. Second, on the repayment amount: I defer to Maya's $275,000 figure, which she has confirmed with controllership, and I recommend we commit to that full amount. I have no basis to dispute it from an employment-law perspective. Third, on the executive-interview protocol: given my confirmation this morning that the implicated VP has retained separate counsel and will not participate without that counsel's written consent, I recommend we adopt a protocol that formally conditions the VP's interview on receipt of written consent from his counsel, sets a reasonable outer deadline — say 30 days from today — so we are not indefinitely delayed, and designates a fallback witness from the distributor-management team who can speak to the relevant relationships if the VP remains unavailable. I also recommend we document our good-faith outreach to the VP's counsel in writing so the record reflects that any delay is not of our making. Those are my final recommendations on all three open items, Elena.
